title: Projection-normalized projective-line adjunction over any affine base
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $N\geq1$ satisfy $NA=0$, and let $S$ be any affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme] on which $N$ is invertible in every local ring. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ in the standard-chart homogeneous coordinates $\operatorname{Option}(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(1)))$, with projection $q:P\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Work in the ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use exact inverse image $q^*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Put $B=A_P(1)[2]$, where $A_P(1)=\mu_{N,P}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_P}A_P$ with roots-of-unity action as in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For $F=Rq_*$ use the canonical projection isomorphisms $\mathrm{PF}_{M,K}:FM\otimes_A^LK\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M\otimes_A^Lq^*K)$ of [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection] with factorization $(\mathrm{id}_P,q)$. There exist a derived morphism $t:FB\to A_S$ and an adjunction $F\dashv H$, where $HK=B\otimes_A^Lq^*K$, whose actual counit, for every unbounded $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, is
$$\epsilon^H_K:F(B\otimes_A^Lq^*K)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{B,K}^{-1}}FB\otimes_A^LK\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}A_S\otimes_A^LK\xrightarrow{\lambda_K}K.$$
No Noetherian, constructibility, boundedness or Tor-amplitude assumption is imposed. At $K=A_S$ the formula identifies the counit with $t$, using the canonical unit identifications.

old_proof.text:
Let $B_T=A_T(1)[2]$ for $T=S,P,W$, where $W=P	imes_SP$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:P	o W$. Apply [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals] to $N,A$ and the scheme $S$; no Noetherian hypothesis is required there. It gives the isomorphism $b_S$ and the trace $t:=t_S=\operatorname{pr}_2b_S^{-1}:Rq_*B_P	o A_S$, and, identifying each $p_i$ with $r_P:\mathbf P^1_P	o P$, the trace $t_i:=t_P:Rp_{i*}B_W	o A_P$. Its base-change clause for $v=q:P	o S$ carries $t_S$ to $t_P$ under the canonical proper exchange and the twist pullback identification [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For $p_1$ the base-change square is $W\xrightarrow{p_2}P$ over $q$, whose exchange is $ eta_1:q^*Rq_*	o Rp_{1*}p_2^*$; for $p_2$ it is the swapped square, with exchange $ eta_2:q^*Rq_*	o Rp_{2*}p_1^*$. Hence
$$t_i\circ eta_{i,B_P}=q^*t\quad(i=1,2),$$
under $q^*B_S=B_P$, $p_{3-i}^*B_P=B_W$ and $q^*A_S=A_P$. The same node states that $\Delta$ is an effective Cartier divisor, with supported Kummer morphism $\delta:R\Delta_*A_P	o B_W$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], and that, with $\alpha_i:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{i*}R\Delta_*A_P$ the derived-composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$,
$$s_i:=t_iRp_{i*}(\delta)\alpha_i=1_{A_P}\quad(i=1,2).$$
These are equations of derived morphisms over the given, possibly non-Noetherian, base.

old_proof.text:
Write $F=Rq_*$ and temporarily $G(K)=q^*K\otimes B_P$. The maps $q,p_i$ are proper projective lines by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The Cartier diagonal is closed [lem-amb-p1-diagonal-cartier] and hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Thus [lem-kun-0f0g] gives all the projection isomorphisms below, including those for $\Delta$, on whole unbounded categories. With the normalized comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], define
$$v_M:R\Delta_*M\cong p_1^*M\otimes R\Delta_*A_P\xrightarrow{1\otimes\delta}p_1^*M\otimes B_W.$$
The first identification uses $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$. Put
$$\eta_M:M\cong Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*M\xrightarrow{Rp_{2*}v_M}Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes B_W)\xrightarrow{C_M}GFM,$$
where $C_M$ is inverse projection for $p_2$, followed by $\beta_{2,M}^{-1}\otimes1$. All arrows are natural in $M$. Define the natural transformation
$$e_K:FGK\xrightarrow{\pi_{q,K,B_P}^{-1}}K\otimes FB_P\xrightarrow{1\otimes t}K\otimes A_S\longrightarrow K.$$
The ordered map $\pi$ is the symmetry-conjugate of the canonical PF of the item, exactly as in [def-kun-projection-formula-map].

old_proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-etale-coordinate-trace-contractions] with $f=q$, $J_S=A_S(1)$, and $d=1$. The line hypothesis is [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]; step 1 supplies precisely both trace-exchange equations. It gives
$$e_{FM}F(C_M)=F(1_M\otimes t_1)F(\pi_{p_1,M,B_W}^{-1}).$$
Precompose with $FRp_{2*}(v_M)$, identifying $FRp_{2*}=FRp_{1*}$. Naturality of projection in its inside factor, and its section identity for $p_1\Delta=1$ in [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition], identify
$$\pi_{p_1,M,B_W}^{-1}Rp_{1*}(v_M)=(1_M\otimes Rp_{1*}\delta)\,(1_M\otimes\alpha_1)$$
under $Rp_{1*}R\Delta_*M=M$ and the tensor unit constraints. Consequently
$$e_{FM}F(\eta_M)=F(1_M\otimes s_1)=1_{FM},$$
by step 1. All these are equations of canonical derived arrows.

The second equation of [lem-sfb-etale-coordinate-trace-contractions] says
$$G(e_K)C_{GK}=(1_{GK}\otimes t_2)\pi_{p_2,GK,B_W}^{-1}.$$
Here $p_1^*GK=p_2^*GK$: both equal the pullback from $S$ of $K\otimes B_S$. Precompose with $Rp_{2*}(v_{GK})$. The section identity and naturality of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition], now for $p_2\Delta=1$, give
$$\pi_{p_2,GK,B_W}^{-1}Rp_{2*}(v_{GK})=(1_{GK}\otimes Rp_{2*}\delta)(1_{GK}\otimes\alpha_2).$$
Thus $G(e_K)\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}\otimes s_2=1_{GK}$ by step 1. The line self-symmetry used in the coordinate comparison is identity: on a trivializing etale cover $ae\otimes be\mapsto be\otimes ae=ab(e\otimes e)$. Its shift is $2$, so swapping it past degree $j$ gives $(-1)^{2j}=1$. No truncation of $K$ or $M$ occurs.

old_proof.text: For completeness construct the adjunction with this actual $e$. Send $u:FM\to K$ to $G(u)\eta_M$ and $v:M\to GK$ to $e_KF(v)$. These operations are natural. Their first composite is $e_KFG(u)F\eta_M=u\,e_{FM}F\eta_M=u$, by naturality of $e$ and step 3. Their second is $G(e_K)GF(v)\eta_M=G(e_K)\eta_{GK}v=v$, by naturality of $\eta$ and step 4. Hence they are inverse natural Hom bijections and [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives $F\dashv G$; the counit at $K$ is the image of $1_{GK}$ under the second bijection, namely $e_K$.

old_proof.text:
The symmetry isomorphism $h_K:B_P\otimes q^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*K\otimes B_P$ identifies the functor $H$ in the item with $G$. Use the preceding Hom bijection followed by $h_K^{-1}$ to give $F\dashv H$. Its actual counit is $e_KF(h_K)$. By the definition of the ordered projection map and the natural symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym], this is
$$F(B_P\otimes q^*K)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{B_P,K}^{-1}}FB_P\otimes K\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}A_S\otimes K\xrightarrow{\lambda_K}K.$$
The canonical compactification PF with $(1_P,q)$ is this same proper counit-defined map by [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. At $K=A_S$, projection with the tensor unit is the canonical unit identification: its adjunct is the original pullback counit, by [def-kun-projection-formula-map]; the adjunction triangle therefore identifies its mate with the unit constraint. Naturality of the unitors and [lem-kun-tensor-unit] make the displayed counit exactly $t$. If $N=1$, then $A=0$ and every object and arrow is the unique one in its zero derived category; the formula still holds. The empty affine base is harmless. No Noetherian hypothesis was used anywhere; all exchange, projection and coordinate identities hold for arbitrary bases and unbounded complexes.
